analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches and supplied source excerpts. These units change documentation only; no independently supported security regression was identified. changelog.d/cluster-auto-update.md:3-10 describes default-on coordinated release staging, bounded request draining, restart, health promotion, rollback/quarantine and a bounded executable version probe. docs/architecture/inference.md:2966-2970 (head patch coordinates) adds matching worker builds as a prerequisite for re-planning after staggered restarts, avoiding a documented 600-second failure delay.
Relevant contracts are artifact integrity and qualification (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054), replaceable-binary rollback authority (T-043), request cancellation/resource retirement (T-010), serving availability (A-018), and fresh connection-bound authorization after restart (T-053). The documentation does not establish how these controls are implemented. Integration should verify release verification before staging or executing the version probe, authenticated peer/update readiness bound to the exact release and pairing, admission fencing and complete native retirement before restart, rollback behavior across unequal peer outcomes, and renewed authorization rather than reuse of old grants. Examine ClusterService, ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild and the update/watchdog implementations when supplied; neither missing implementation nor an imagined older deployment supports a finding here.
The unchanged inference excerpts (lines 1-837) describe request validation, memory admission, authenticated pair handoffs, tenant cache scoping, media bounds and native retirement. They provide interaction context, not evidence that this PR modifies encryption, cache policy (T-041), data exposure or billing. Implementation coverage remains material to validating the new update lifecycle claims.
